body.p: In response to the Final Office Action dated June 20, 2024, Claims 1 and 13 have been amended. No new matter is believed to have been added by way of these amendments.
Accordingly, Claims 1-24 are currently pending for consideration. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration in view of the remarks set forth below.
A. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. §101

The following remarks are not to be used for claim construction or any other similar purpose, but are presented solely in connection with the § 101 analysis. Applicant further reserves the rights to make additional arguments.

The Office Action asserts that the claims were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 because the claims are allegedly directed to non-statutory subject matter. Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejection and disagrees that the claims are directed to an abstract idea, as alleged by the Office. However, Applicant has amended Claim 1 to expedite allowance. Claim 1 has been amended to recite that "the travelling assistance unit performs the assistance operation of assisting travelling of the vehicle based on the object information", which recites a practical application to the alleged abstract idea (a point which Applicant does not concede). Reconsideration in view of the above amendments is respectfully requested.
B. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103
Claims 1-24 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over JP 2009- 83647 A to Suzuki et al. (hereinafter "Suzuki") in view of U.S. 2018/0093663 to Kim et al. (hereinafter "Kim").
1. Rationale of 35 U.S.C. § 103

The Patent and Trademark Office has the burden under 35 U.S.C. § 103 to establish a prima facie case of obviousness. The rationale to support a conclusion that the claim would have been obvious is that all the claimed elements were known in the prior art and one skilled in the art could have combined the elements as claimed by known methods with no change in their respective functions, and the combination yielded nothing more than predictable results to one of ordinary skill in the art. It can be important to identify a reason that would have prompted a person of ordinary skill in the relevant field to combine the elements in the way the claimed new subject

2. Independent Claim 1
Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejection of Claim 1 but has amended the claim to expedite allowance. As amended, Claim 1 recites in part:

determine storage priority of the object information in the object information storage unit based on the priority region of assistance operation; and manage a storage state of the object information in the object information storage unit based on the storage priority, wherein
the travelling assistance unit performs the assistance operation of assisting
travelling of the vehicle based on the object information.
Applicant respectfully asserts that Suzuki and Kim, alone or in combination, fail to disclose at least the above feature(s) of amended Claim 1.

For example, Applicant respectfully asserts that the references fail to teach the feature(s) "a priority region", to "obtain a priority region of assistance operation" and, further, to "manage a storage state of the object information in the object information storage unit based on the storage priority".

In the rejection of Claim 1, the Office asserts that Suzuki teaches the feature(s) to "determine storage priority of the object information in the object information storage unit based on the type of assistance operation" (See at least "the object information necessary for the control system is given priority by storing the object information of the object other than the separation moving object, that is, the object information of the approaching movement object and the stop object in preference to the object information of the separation movement object").

In Suzuki, the order in which object information is stored is determined based on the time to collision (TTC) with the object, hence, "the object information of the approaching movement object and the stop object in preference to the object information of the separation movement object", as asserted by the Office. See also Suzuki, page 4 ("In this case, it is preferable to store the object information with priority in the order of short collision time TTC. Thereby, the object detection process can be performed in the order of the shortest collision time TTC."). Accordingly,

if Suzuki teaches that the order of priority is based on TTC, Applicant respectfully asserts that Suzuki does not teach "a priority region" and to "obtain a priority region of assistance operation". That is, an order of priority based on TTC cannot reasonably be interpreted as teaching "a priority region", to "obtain a priority region of assistance operation" and, further, to "manage a storage state of the object information in the object information storage unit based on the storage priority", as recited in amended Claim 1.
Kim also fails to remedy the deficiencies of Suzuki.

Therefore, for at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully asserts that Suzuki and Kim, alone or in combination, fail to disclose each and every feature of amended Claim 1. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.
3. Independent Claim 13
Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejection of Claim 13 but has been amended the claim to expedite allowance. Claim 13 has been amended similarly as Claim 1.

Therefore, for at least the same reasons as asserted above with respect to amended Claim 1, Applicant respectfully asserts that Suzuki and Kim, alone or in combination, fail to disclose each and every feature of amended Claim 13. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.
4. Dependent Claims 2-12 and 14-24

Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejections but submits that each of the dependent Claims 2-12 and 14-24 depends directly or indirectly on independent Claims 1 and 13. Thus, dependent Claims 2-12 and 14-24 incorporate by reference all the features of independent Claims 1 and 13. In view of the features as recited in the independent Claims 1 and 13, and in view of the additional features as recited in the dependent claims, Applicant respectfully submits that dependent Claims 2-12 and 14-24 are allowable for at least the reasons discussed above and their respective additional novel features. Although Applicant has not discussed specific features of all of the dependent claims in this response, Applicant does not necessarily agree with the characterizations and assessments made by the Examiner with respect to the dependent claims. Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that dependent Claims 2-12 and 14-24 are allowable.

C. No Disclaimers or Disavowals

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application.
